subject: POC scope and reservation guarantees — next tests and decision criteria
messages:
From: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.ai>
To: Julian Park <julian.park@heliontx.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 29 Jun 2027 16:12:00 -0700
Subject: POC scope and reservation guarantees — next tests and decision criteria

Julian / team — thanks again for the call earlier. Quick written recap and proposed next steps so we have a single place to track decisions. High level takeaways: 

- Helion is evaluating dedicated (reserved) capacity vs hyperscaler-managed GPU endpoints for inference. Primary drivers: p99 latency under load, predictable unit cost, and capacity guarantees during scheduled and bursty events.
- Immediate ask from your side: head-to-head POC that proves reservation guarantees under production-like traffic and validates fallback behavior to a cross-region/hyperscaler option.

What Redwood will provide for the POC:
- Dedicated GPU pool (single-tenant) with reservation sizing options (monthly vs annual commit).
- Autoscale-burst policy: primary reservation + configured burst into shared capacity with explicit fallback policy (we will demonstrate failover sequencing).
- Observability: per-route latency histograms, token-level cost, KV-cache hit rates.

Open questions / what we need from Helion to scope the POC:
1) Target sustained throughput and peak burst RPS you want us to validate (please confirm steady-state and spike profile).
2) Which model variants you plan to test (e.g., 30B quantized, 7B fp16) and sequence length distribution.
3) Any maintenance window constraints or blackout periods.
4) Procurement preference for reserve term (monthly vs 12mo) and preferred billing contact.

Proposed next steps (short timeline):
- You confirm throughput/model list and preferred test week (we suggest Jul 12–16).
- We share a test matrix (latency/throughput/99th/tail) + SLA/fallback playbook.
- Procurement reviews PO template; we do a short kickoff call week of Jul 5 to align runbook.

I've attached a draft test matrix and SLA playbook for initial review; will update after you confirm the target RPS.

Thanks — looking forward to proving the tail behavior for you.

Connor O'Brien
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
connor.obrien@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0198
Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood_reserved_vs_hyperscaler_matrix.xlsx (spreadsheet), sla-fallback-playbook.pdf (summary)
From: Julian Park <julian.park@heliontx.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.ai>
Cc: procure@heliontx.com
Date: Wed, 30 Jun 2027 09:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: POC scope and reservation guarantees — next tests and decision criteria

Connor — thanks for the clear recap. A few clarifying questions before we lock dates: 

1) Guarantees vs preemption: for a "reserved" pool, will Helion see any preemption during cloud provider maintenance or hardware reboots, or is reserved = single-tenant GPU allocation we control? If there is a shared-burst fallback, what is the contractual SLA during fallback?
2) Billing/commit: our finance team prefers a quarterly commitment if possible. Do you offer 3-month reserved terms or only monthly/annual? Any early-termination credit model?
3) Failover sequencing: if you fail to meet p99 guaranteed latency, what's the automatic fallback path (another Redwood variant, hyperscaler endpoint, or cross-region)? We need a deterministic failover we can code to.
4) Security: we'll need an outline of data isolation, logs/audit access, and KMS integration for the POC (we won't share PHI but want to validate key handling).

For throughput: initial target is 150 rps sustained with 1:3 spike pattern to 450 rps (30s spike windows). Models: 7B fp16 and 30B quantized. Sequence lengths average 256 tokens with bursts to 1024 for long-form generation.

Procurement loop (procure@heliontx.com) — please advise who owns the PO template. I'll plan for the Jul 12–16 window but would like to confirm the failover SLA and reserved-vs-burst billing model first.

—Julian
Julian Park
Head of Product, Helion Therapeutics
julian.park@heliontx.com
From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 30 Jun 2027 11:20:00 -0700
Subject: RE: POC scope and reservation guarantees — next tests and decision criteria

Connor — internal note / proposed answers to send to Helion (I can send or you can). Summarized responses to Julian's questions below.

1) Preemption / reservation semantics: Redwood Dedicated offers single-tenant reserved pools (no preemption) when customers take a reserved SKU (monthly or annual commit). For customers that want capacity flexibility we offer a hybrid: reserved primary + autoscale burst into a shared capacity pool that is best-effort. When we describe "burst" we explicitly provide the fallback SLA for that path (lower p99 guarantee and best-effort availability).

2) Billing terms: we support monthly and annual reservation contracts today. We do not have a standard 3-month cadence, but for POCs we can offer a bridging monthly commitment with a credit applied if you convert to an annual commitment within 60 days. Karthik — can you confirm the economics for a short-term bridge credit and provide a simple example for Julian?

3) Failover sequencing (example):
- Primary: Reserved single-tenant pool (p99 target X ms)
- Automatic fallback: compatible quantized variant in Redwood shared pool (lower performance, documented p99)
- Final fallback (optional): route to a customer-supplied hyperscaler endpoint — we can implement a deterministic routing policy that is configured at rollout time.

4) Security: Laura will attach our KMS/HSM integration brief and an audit-log sample. For the POC we can provide scoped logs and ephemeral key access. Laura — can you pull the Helion-specific KMS notes and the audit sample we used for other medtech customers?

Proposed test matrix (high level) to send to Helion:
- Sustained throughput: 150 rps steady-state (target)
- Spike profile: 450 rps for 30s windows
- Models: 7B fp16, 30B quantized
- Metrics: p50 / p95 / p99 latency, error rate, KV-cache hit rate, and failover latency when we trigger fallback.

I'll hold on sending until Karthik confirms economics and Laura adds security appendix. If you want, I can send this draft directly to Julian with our attachments.

—Monica
Monica Patel
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
monica.patel@redwood.ai

Date: Thu, 01 Jul 2027 08:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: POC scope and reservation guarantees — next tests and decision criteria

Julian — thanks for the details; we've confirmed internally and attached the matrix and SLA playbook Monica referenced. Short answers up front: 

- Reservation semantics: reserved = single-tenant GPUs for the duration of the term (no preemption). Burst path is an optional configured policy; when active it is best-effort and we document the fallback p99.
- Billing: we can do a monthly bridge commitment with a conversion credit if you convert to a 12mo within 60 days. Karthik has included a sample pricing table in the spreadsheet.
- Failover sequencing: we will implement deterministic routing you can read at deploy time (Primary -> Redwood shared fallback -> customer hyperscaler endpoint). We'll ship a small SDK stub so your infra can detect and act on the active tier.

Proposed POC plan (tentative):
- Run dates: Jul 12–16 (5 business days); kickoff call Jul 8 to walk runbook.
- Targets: sustained 150 rps, spikes to 450 rps (30s windows).
- Models: 7B fp16 and 30B quantized (we'll run both under the same traffic profile).
- Acceptance criteria: p99 <= 800ms for reserved pool under sustained load, failover behavior documented and repeatable, KV cache hit >= 60% (if you enable caching).

Attachments: redwood_reserved_vs_hyperscaler_matrix.xlsx (pricing + test matrix), sla-fallback-playbook.pdf (playbook). I've also attached a PO template (po-template.docx) for procurement to review. Links: https://app.hubspot.com/deals/678901/HLN-2026-042 and the Drive folder with test scripts.

Can you confirm: (1) test week (Jul 12–16) is good, (2) procurement can review PO template and send back comments, and (3) a short kickoff Jul 8 works for your ops/product team?

Connor O'Brien
